title: October DC hardening: LDAP binds now need an ldap/ SPN ticket, breaking NetApp ONTAP and Azure NetApp Files with session security 'none' (KB5134907)
summary: Since the 13 October 2026 Windows security updates, domain controllers only accept Kerberos authentication to LDAP with a service ticket that matches the DC's registered LDAP SPN. Azure NetApp Files and NetApp ONTAP with AD LDAP client session security set to none bind with a cifs/<dc-fqdn> ticket instead, so the DC rejects the bind: SMB share access can fail, new SMB volumes fail with 'Invalid credentials', and name mapping and user/group lookups break. Microsoft re-flagged it in MC1551001 on 12 November 2026.
why: This is a Kerberos ticket-to-service binding check, the kind of hardening that closes SPN-swapping abuse against LDAP. The only DC-side workaround, `LdapSPNVerificationLevel=0`, switches the check off for every caller on that DC, so it is a temporary exception, not a fix. Any other appliance that binds to LDAP with a non-LDAP service ticket can fail the same way.
todo: Self-managed ONTAP: set session-security-for-ad-ldap to sign or seal on each affected SVM (ONTAP then requests an ldap/ ticket), after checking NetApp's current guidance.
Azure NetApp Files: follow KB5134907 and NetApp's KB until NetApp ships its resolution.

If you must use `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters\LdapSPNVerificationLevel = 0` (applies without restart), scope it to as few DCs as possible, record an owner and end date, and set it back to 1.
Use the same window to check that LDAP signing and channel binding are enforced on every DC.
effective_note: Enforced by the 13 October 2026 Windows Server updates and later; NetApp resolution for Azure NetApp Files not yet available on 13 November.
